chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Muskan from Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I was in the presence of Ziyad ibn Abdillah, and with him was Rabi'ah al-Ra'i. So Ziyad said, 'What did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sanctify from Medina?' He said to him, 'A Bareed, in a Bareed.' So he said to Rabi'ah, 'And it was many miles in the era of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' So he was silent and did not answer him. So Ziyad turned towards me and said, 'O Abu Abdillah, what are you saying?'

So I said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sanctified from Medina what is between its two Labeets.' He said, 'And what is between the two Labeets?' I said, 'What is encompassed by the heat (hills/area).' He said, 'And what did he sanctify from the trees?' I said, 'From 'Ayyr to Wu'ayr.'

Safwan said, Ibn Muskan said, Al-Hasan said, 'A person asked him while I was seated, so he said to him, 'And what is between the two Labeets?' He said, 'What is between the two Saurayn to the Saniyya.'

key_terms.الْحِرَار: The heat / The encompassed area (referring to the city's extent)
key_terms.حَرَّمَ: Sanctified / Made forbidden (to hunt or cut trees)
key_terms.عَيْرٍ إِلَى وُعَيْر: From 'Ayyr to Wu'ayr (specific tree types or landmarks)
key_terms.لَابَتَيْهَا: Its two Labeets (landmarks/hills defining the boundary)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific boundaries of the sanctified area of Medina according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the precise geographical boundaries of Medina's Haram, a topic of significant jurisprudential debate regarding the extent of its sanctity and the prohibition of hunting or cutting trees within it. The narration highlights the Imam's direct engagement with Ziyad ibn Abd al-Malik, the Umayyad governor, demonstrating the transmission of prophetic tradition through both oral clarification and written correspondence ('barid'). The specific landmarks mentioned, such as the 'Labeets' and 'Saurayn', serve as critical markers in Shia fiqh for determining the legal status of the city's surroundings.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Al Hassan Al Sayqal who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> was in the presence of Ziyad Bin Abdullah, and with him was Rabi’a Al-Rai’e. So Ziyad said, ‘What is which Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> sanctified from Al-Medina?’ So he said, ‘An area of Bareyd’. So he said to Rabi’e, ‘And it was many miles in the era of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’. So he was silent and did not answer him. So Ziyad turned towards me<sup>asws</sup>, and he said, ‘O Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>! What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying?’

So I<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> sanctified from Al-Medina what is in between the two Labeets’. He said, ‘And what is in between the two Labeets?’ I<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is encompassed by the hills’. He said, ‘And what did he<sup>saww</sup> sanctify from the trees?’ I said, ‘From this hill to that hill’.

Safwan said, ‘Ibn Muskan said, ‘Al-Hassan said, ‘A person asked him<sup>asws</sup> and I was seated, so he said to him, ‘And what is in between the two Labeets?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is between the two boundaries of Al-Saniyya’.
en.sarwar: 3. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from ibn Muskan from al-Hassan al- Sayqal who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Once I was in the meeting of Ziyad ibn ‘Abd Allah and Rabi’ah al-Ra’iy was also there. Ziyad said, ‘What is the area which the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has made a place of sacred status in al-Madinah?’ He replied, ‘It is one square Barid.’ He then said to Rabi’ah, ‘During the time of the Messenger of Allah it was many miles.’ He then remained quiet and did not answer him. Ziyad then turned to me and asked, ‘O abu ‘Abd Allah, what do you say?’

I replied, ‘The sacred area of the Messenger of Allah is the area between the two Labit of al-Madinah.’ He then asked, ‘What is al-Labit?’ I replied, ‘It is the area surrounded by al-Hirar (hills).’ He asked, ‘What of amount of trees has he made sacred?’ I said, ‘From this mountain to that mountain.’”

“Safwan has said that ibn Muskan has said that al-Hassan has said, ‘A man then asked him, when I was present, ‘Is it what is between the two hills?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘It is the area between the two boundaries up to al-Thaniyah (name of a place).”’
